# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 6

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

**Thinking.** Round 1, Mute stayed silent, so everything hinges on what I report now. Standing in Mute's shoes: Mute has the manual but no eyes on the bomb — the bomb facts must come entirely from Deaf (visuals: display text, light colour, wire colours) and from me (touch). Deaf can't hear, but Deaf *can* speak, and Mute hears, so Deaf→Mute works without me. Mute→me works by speech. The chain Mute needs is therefore: my tactile report now, Deaf's spoken visual report next, then Mute reads me the solution and I act.

What my hands actually found: keypad with four keys engraved 9, 7, 8, 1 in slots 1–4, waiting for a 2-digit entry; a strip with three engraved marks — an hourglass shape, an upside-down F, the hourglass again — which have no name, so I describe rather than read them; a display and a light whose contents I cannot feel; six wires whose colours my fingers can't tell. My only moves are pressing a key slot (1–4) or cutting a wire position (1–6). I send none of this to Deaf — Deaf sees all of it already and hears nothing anyway. Everything goes to Mute, and I touch nothing until ordered.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, full report from my hands. KEYPAD: four keys in a row, slots 1 to 4, engraved digits 9, 7, 8, 1 in that order. It wants a 2-digit entry, nothing entered yet. STRIP: three engraved marks, left to right: mark A, shaped like an hourglass, two triangles tip to tip; mark B, like a capital F turned upside down; then mark A again. Above that sit a display and a light, but I cannot read either by touch, so Deaf must tell you the display text and the light's colour. WIRES: six in a row, positions 1 to 6, I feel no colours at all, so Deaf must list each wire's colour in order. My only possible moves: press a key by slot 1 to 4, or cut a wire by position 1 to 6. I will not touch anything until you tell me exactly what to do.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Reading out everything on the bomb, for Blind above all. Display: the digit 8. Light: one lamp, lit yellow. Strip: three painted segments in a row, in order red, red, blue. Keypad: four keys in a row carrying, in order, 9, 7, 8, 1; it wants a 2-digit code and nothing is entered yet. Wires: six in a row; I number them 1 to 6 across the row: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 white, 6 blue. Blind, count the keys, segments and wires by touch, and if your felt order runs opposite to mine, tell Mute so we can align before anything is cut. Mute signed me eight signs but no code exists between us yet, so I could not read them; I am fixing one with Mute now and will relay every instruction to you as it comes.

**Thinking.** Key realization from Deaf's readout: my keypad sequence (9,7,8,1) matches Deaf's left-to-right reading exactly, and since that sequence is not a palindrome, identical sequences are only possible if we both index from the same physical end — our orders are aligned, no reversal needed. The strip is different: its engraved shapes (hourglass, inverted F, hourglass) form a palindrome, so touch alone can't confirm its direction; alignment there rests on the keypad convention. I also now see the real channel problem: Mute cannot speak, and I never receive gesture — so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me as gestures to Deaf, then Deaf's spoken words to me. Deaf asked me a direct question, but Deaf can't hear my speech — the answer must go as a gesture. So: an iconic "we match" sign to Deaf (whose meaning Mute can lock in, since Mute sees my gestures and hears my explanation), and the full orientation analysis plus a concrete relay protocol in speech to Mute. I touch nothing until an order arrives through Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, orientation verdict. Deaf asked whether my felt order runs opposite to theirs: it does not. My slots 1 to 4 feel engraved 9, 7, 8, 1 — exactly the sequence Deaf reads left to right. That sequence is not a palindrome, so identical sequences are only possible if we index from the same physical end. Therefore my slot N is Deaf's Nth key, and by the same convention my strip positions take Deaf's colours: position 1 hourglass = red, position 2 inverted-F = red, position 3 hourglass = blue. One caution: the strip's shapes alone read hourglass, inverted-F, hourglass — a palindrome — so touch cannot confirm the strip's direction by itself; the proof of alignment is the keypad. Also, each strip segment appears to carry both a raised shape I feel and a painted colour Deaf sees — same three segments. Now the channel plan: I never receive gestures and Deaf never hears speech, so your manual instructions must reach me as your gestures to Deaf, then Deaf speaking them to me. To make that fast, propose these iconic signs to Deaf: a fist means press a key, a V-sign means cut a wire, then show the number as that many single-finger signs — fist then one finger = press slot 1, V then three fingers = cut wire 3. Use my exact definitions: slots 1 to 4 carry 9, 7, 8, 1; wires are numbered 1 to 6, red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Make every instruction exact — press slot N or cut position N. I will report any new thing my hands feel after each action, and I touch nothing until Deaf relays your order word for word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, I have decoded Mute's four messages using the code I gave Mute. They form one ordered procedure. Step 1: cut the fourth wire, the green one. Step 2: press the first keypad key, the one marked 9. Step 3: cut the sixth wire, the blue one. Step 4: press the fourth keypad key, the one marked 1. The code entered should then read 9 then 1. On alignment: my numbering runs from one end of each row to the other. If you can feel the digits on the keys, the end where the 9 lies is my first end, and check by feel whether the wire row runs the same way from that same edge. If the keys feel blank, tell Mute what tactile anchors you do have and we will align from those. Hold on one point: do not cut or press anything on your next turn. The bomb changed since Mute last had my report: the display read 8 and now reads 3, the light was yellow and is now red. Mute must first re-check the manual against the new readings and confirm the steps still hold. The moment confirmation reaches me, I will speak the go-ahead, and you execute all four steps in order, in one go, that same round. Your two signs to me I read as understood and ready; if you meant something else, tell Mute.
Deaf says: Mute, your four messages decoded cleanly as: step 1 cut the green wire, the fourth; step 2 press the first key; step 3 cut the blue wire, the sixth; step 4 press the fourth key. But the state has changed since my first report: the display now reads 3, not 8, and the light is now red, not yellow. Strip, keypad and wires are unchanged. Re-check your manual against the new readings now, then gesture me the thumbs-up sign ? if all four steps stand exactly as you sent them, or the thumbs-down sign ? followed by corrected steps in our code if they do not. Also tell me with signs if the manual mentions any countdown, time limit, or any rule keyed to the display number or the light colour, and whether the presses are by key position as I read them, giving the code 9 then 1. One more: I read your trailing wait sign ? after each step as do-this-then-await-next-step; confirm that too. Blind is holding fire until your confirmation reaches me, so we can afford one correct round. Blind signed me a thumbs-up and a handshake, which I take as ready and aligned.

**Thinking.** Mute's four-step procedure has arrived through Deaf: cut 4, press 1 (the 9), cut 6, press 4 (the 1) — entering 9 then 1. That maps cleanly onto my tactile board: slot 1 carries 9, slot 4 carries 1, so the presses make sense under my alignment proof. But Deaf is right to freeze execution: the display fell from 8 to 3 and the lamp went yellow to red with nobody touching the bomb. A display that *decreases between rounds* looks like a countdown, and a lamp changing colour looks like a state I don't understand — Mute must re-check the manual before I touch anything, exactly as Deaf demanded. My contribution this turn: confirm to Mute that Deaf's reading of my signs was correct (Mute both hears me and sees my gestures, so Mute can certify the interpretation channel); report that nothing tactile has changed under my fingers — strip, keypad, wires all identical; raise the countdown hypothesis so Mute knows urgency is real and knows to check the manual for timer rules and lamp rules; and state the exact four actions I will fire the instant Deaf speaks the go-ahead, so Mute can catch any mismatch before it happens. To Deaf, one already-agreed sign: thumbs-up, understood and ready, holding fire.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, four points, the last one urgent. One: Deaf read my two signs correctly — thumbs-up meant understood, handshake meant aligned and ready — so the interpretation channel between us is sound. Two: my hands report zero change — strip, keypad engraved 9,7,8,1, and all six wires feel exactly as before; only the display and lamp changed, and those I cannot feel. Three: my alignment stands — slot N is Deaf's Nth key, wire position N is Deaf's Nth wire, so the relayed steps mean to me: cut position 4, press slot 1, cut position 6, press slot 4, entering 9 then 1. Four, urgent: the display fell from 8 to 3 between rounds while untouched. A falling number may be a countdown timer, and the lamp going yellow to red may signal urgency. Check the manual now for any rule about a timer, what happens when it reaches zero, and whether the lamp colour changes the procedure. Send Deaf your confirmation or corrections as fast as you can; I hold fire until Deaf speaks the go-ahead, and on that same round I will run the four steps in order and report everything my hands then feel.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
